newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says NZ economy worse than govt argued.
newsitem.headline: Peters says NZ economy worse than govt argued.

text.p: New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters said on Tuesday the economy was in a worse state than the conservative National Party government was arguing before last month's general election.

"We constructed our economic statement (in July) on a very conservative scenario. We thought the economy was in a worse state than the government was arguing. We still believe that to be the case, and we are asking for the absolute up-to-date position currently from independent sources other than Treasury," he told a news conference.
Peters declined to say from whom he was seeking the information, but said he expected to have it by Friday.

Nationalist New Zealand First holds the balance of power between National, which remains as caretaker government, and the centre-left Labour Party, and is negotiating to form a coalition with one of them.
Peters has been a persistent critic of the tightness of monetary policy and the high level of the New Zealand dollar.
